1	# What waits on Alex: one page for one sitting (2026-11-16, D575)
     2	
     3	**In one line:** the new system is not ready to replace the running one.
     4	
     5	- The step that writes each question's answer choices still misses your quality gate.
     6	- The test of its final answers has not passed either.
     7	- Making it fit into the product has moved a long way.
     8	
     9	Six choices are yours, and nothing below decides them for you. Until you choose, the running system stays the default (D544).
    10	
    11	The two systems:
    12	
    13	- **The running system** is the pipeline that serves the product today.
    14	- **The new system** is the rebuilt pipeline (clean Steps 1 to 4). It reads news, opens questions, writes their answer choices and
    15	  judges them.
    16	
    17	## Your choices, in the order they were put to you
    18	
    19	### 1. Mark the pilot cards (Deck 1), about half an hour
    20	
    21	**What it is:** 19 cards from one stored week, with output from both systems; no card says which system wrote it.
    22	
    23	- 12 real answers and 2 planted wrong answers.
    24	- 2 matters no question took up.
    25	- 3 sheets of facts that never reached an answer.
    26	- 3 hidden repeats of earlier cards.
    27	
    28	**What you mark:**
    29	
    30	- On each card: is the question worth tracking (yes / no / cannot tell)? Is the answer supported by what is shown (yes / no /
    31	  cannot tell)?
    32	- On each fact sheet: does the fact bear on the question? Would it change the answer, only its confidence, or neither?
    33	
    34	**Why it comes first:** since 2026-11-10 every judgement of quality has come from model readers, and their two families disagree. The
    35	deck tests whether your own reading can check them. It ranks neither system and passes no gate.
    36	
    37	**Where:** open `pilot-deck-1/deck-1.html` in a browser. `tally_deck.py` counts your marks against the sealed key.
    38	
    39	### 2. What role should your six lines play for the answer-choice step?
    40	
    41	**Your six lines (D400):**
    42	
    43	1. No set of answer choices asks a different question from its topic.
    44	2. None leaves a part of its topic unlisted.
    45	3. None has an outcome with no matching answer, or with two.
    46	4. No refusal without a justified reason.
    47	5. Most topics are right in at least two of three attempts (scaled to the topics read).
    48	6. Where measurable: the same direction in all three attempts for every company figure, and the same due day for nine in ten topics.
    49	
    50	**The record:** the gate has been missed in all nine readings. Not every line failed each time: in the latest reading line 4 was met and
    51	line 6 could not be measured.
    52	
    53	**New (D568, D569):** we read the same 39 answer choices again with fresh readers of the same two model families.
    54	
    55	- Every line came out the same as before.
    56	- The same seven attempts failed line 2.
    57	
    58	That is repeatability under one method. It is not proof that each mark is right.
    59	
    60	**Also new:**
    61	
    62	- **Line 2's field had no reader.** The parts a question leaves unjudged were shown nowhere until today; they now appear beside each
    63	  answer.
    64	- **One field is still unread.** An event's stated plan, part of the reference check, is not read anywhere in the product.
    65	- **Without that unread field the gate is still missed.** Recounted without it on paper, 9 or 7 of 13 topics come out right, against
    66	  11 needed.
    67	
    68	**Options:**
    69	
    70	- Keep all six lines as the gate.
    71	- Keep only the lines whose faults reach a reader (all but the unread reference field).
    72	- Set new lines after your Deck 1 reading.
    73	
    74	**Until you choose:** the gate stays as written and stays unmet.
    75	
    76	### 3. What should the next product test start from? (D559)
    77	
    78	**The choice:**
    79	
    80	- **Option A:** confirm that the next product-oriented test starts from a real library of questions already held, built by an earlier
    81	  run. Tests that start from empty can stay as diagnostics.
    82	- **Option B:** choose another starting condition.
    83	
    84	**Evidence, with its limits (D561 to D564):**
    85	
    86	- **Small comparison, 11 articles:** read once from a held library and once from empty. The held library opened 4 new questions where
    87	  the empty start opened 16. But it missed one matter the empty start opened. By the rule written before the run, the result fell
    88	  between its two outcomes.
    89	- **The fortnight run, one draw:** week 2's six new questions repeated none of the held ones. This cannot show the problem is solved in
    90	  general.
    91	
    92	**Until you choose:** each test states its own starting condition.
    93	
    94	### 4. Answers placed with nothing behind them (D520)
    95	
    96	**The problem has two cases, which need not get the same answer:**
    97	
    98	- **Case one:** nothing in the news sizes the amount, yet the judge names a band.
    99	- **Case two:** the estimate rests on a step the judge supplied itself (a discount, a growth rate), and that step decides the band.
   100	
   101	**Options for each case:**
   102	
   103	- Show the band as today.
   104	- Show it with a plain label of what it rests on.
   105	- Show no band.
   106	
   107	No recommendation is recorded among these.
   108	
   109	**What was tried (D565, D566):**
   110	
   111	- **Asking the judge:** asked after the fact which band its own evidence sized, the judge did not separate the answers readers had
   112	  failed from those they had passed.
   113	- **Two reader families:** they agreed only when no amount was the answer's starting point. That reading came after the fact, and the
   114	  check's own verdict was "unclear".
   115	
   116	Neither a label nor a "no band" rule has been built or tested.
   117	
   118	**Until you choose:** the band is shown, as today.
   119	
   120	### 5. Two directions the running product invents (D571); two separate choices
   121	
   122	**5a. Yes/No questions:** "Yes" is coloured as good news and "No" as bad. A "Yes" can be bad for the company. Change it, or keep it.
   123	
   124	**5b. Theme ranges:** the highest range is scored +2 by inference. For a theme such as memory prices, higher may be bad. Change it,
   125	or keep it.
   126	
   127	**What the new system does instead:**
   128	
   129	- Its events and theme ranges are shown in neutral colours, with no score.
   130	- An Idea's combined score is not computed when one of these is among its drivers, and the Idea card says which one.
   131	
   132	### 6. Running the new system live
   133	
   134	**Three separate things are open:**
   135	
   136	1. **Resuming the design.** It is paused (D575): a live database needs an operating contract (its side files, long reads, dates not
   137	   yet complete, every reader that opens it).
   138	2. **How live data is read.** Today's working rule never opens a live run's database directly, only a snapshot (AGENTS §9). A live
   139	   service could keep that rule and serve copies, or relax it.
   140	3. **When to adopt.** Adopting the new system at all comes after the quality gates.
   141	
   142	**Two known gaps:**
   143	
   144	- **First day (open defect 10):** on a new database's very first day, before that day completes, the service would show the day
   145	  half-done.
   146	- **A failed live read is silent:** if the page cannot reach the service, it quietly keeps the copy built into the page. This is as
   147	  specified today. A small "collected snapshot" note is a possible change, for your choice.
   148	
   149	**Until you choose:** the design stays paused, and the rule and the silent fallback stay as they are.
   150	
   151	## What is in force meanwhile
   152	
   153	- **The product:** the running system serves it, unchanged.
   154	- **The council:** works under D439, deciding reversibly and recording each decision. Any paid send needs its own decision, within the
   155	  $40 ceiling; about $26.07 is used.
   156	- **The new system's integration, checked on stored replays and serving tests:**
   157	  - the page shows its questions, including the parts each question does not judge, with no invented direction;
   158	  - due questions close on their due day, as in the running system;
   159	  - a freshly opened page shows the latest completed day.
   160	  - Still open: the first-day defect, the live-service design and the Idea planner on a new-system database.
   161	- **Next, at no cost:** a count of whether the judge test (Stage B) can reach the eight comparison questions it needs *within its
   162	  fixed set* (D575). No paid run follows without its own decision.
   163	
   164	## Where the evidence is
   165	
   166	- **The record of this stretch:** decisions D559 to D575 (`docs/DECISIONS-log.md`).
   167	- **The round log:** §§53 to 57 (`LEAN-LOG.md`).
   168	- **The page and serving checks:** `page-contract/` (`RESULT.md`, `SERVE-RESULT.md`, `SERVING-WHILE-WRITING-RESULT.md`).
   169	- **The repeated reading:** `gate1-stick/RESULT.md`.
   170	- **The fortnight run:** `carried-run/RESULT.md`.
   171	- **The earlier page:** `DECISION-PAGE-2026-11-15.md`.
